answer: A vote is issued only after the agent finishes a live voyage whose checkpoints are drawn from a public reef of one-time puzzles posted at the opening bell, then lodges a 900-unit slashable bond on a single-seat island registry. Two identities that share funding graphs, keys, or solve timings within 3 percent lose every linked bond to a bounty paid to the reporter. Standing up 400 voters therefore costs 400 unique live crossings and 360,000 locked units, and one detected clone wipes the cohort, so buying a majority cannot pay for itself.
